title: The pool filled in
hook: invaders filled the Harmandir's pool with rubbish, and Sikhs vowed to restore it

segments.voice: Yesterday, Baba Deep Singh at his desk at Damdama, copying the Granth letter by letter. Your line was the scholar-warrior. Today, the news that reached that desk.

The water comes first. At the Harmandir there's a wide pool, still and bright, with the temple sitting in the middle of it and its reflection beneath. People walk all the way around; some bathe at the steps. The whole place is built around that water. Now take the water away. Tradition says that when Abdali's commanders held Amritsar, they had the pool filled in with rubbish, earth and filth, and the sacred place was defiled. A messenger rides south with the news.
screen: `A STILL, BRIGHT POOL.` → `THE TEMPLE IN THE MIDDLE.` → `THEN THE RUBBISH.`

segments.voice: Start with what the pool is. Tradition says Guru Ram Das began digging it, and Guru Arjan finished the work and built the Harmandir in its center. Tradition also says the city took its name from it: Amritsar, the pool of amrit, the water of immortality. And Guru Arjan sang about it. In a hymn in the Granth, in paraphrase, he says that God himself stood up to finish the work of his saints, and that the land is lovely and the pool is lovely, filled with nectar-water. So the pool isn't decoration. In Sikh memory it's the Gurus' own work, made by hand and blessed in song. Tradition reads the filling as a message: this is over. The Sikh answer was a vow. Tradition says that when the news reached Damdama, Baba Deep Singh, yesterday's old scholar, swore to free the Harmandir, and set out. Leave the ride for another time; stay with what came after the vow. Restoring a pool isn't one dramatic act. It's baskets. People standing in mud, passing rubble hand to hand, carrying it out, again and again, until the water can come back. Sikhs call that shared physical work for the Guru's house kar seva, the service of the hands. And Sikhs tell of the pool being cleaned by kar seva in later times too, with ordinary people, young and old, carrying out silt in baskets. The vow and the basket belong together. One says it will be made right. The other makes it right, one load at a time. Restore it.
screen: `THE POOL IS THE GURUS' OWN WORK.` · `FILLED IN TO SAY: THIS IS OVER.` · `A VOW TO FREE IT.` · `KAR SEVA: ONE BASKET AT A TIME.` · then, large: `RESTORE IT.`

segments.voice: Look around and choose one small patch that's been let go, a corner of a desk, a shelf, a folder on your screen, and clear just that, slowly, one thing at a time, the way you'd carry one basket. If you can't move, picture it. When it's clear, look at it for one breath, and if you pray, say Waheguru as you finish.
sarovar, the sacred pool. Tradition says invaders filled the one at the Harmandir with rubbish, and Sikhs vowed to restore it, with a vow and then with baskets. Today's word.
Your line: restore it. Big repairs are made of small loads, carried one at a time. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: Why did Sikhs care so much when the pool at Amritsar was filled in?
options: In Sikh memory the pool is the Gurus' own work, dug by hand and praised in Guru Arjan's hymn.
It was the city's only water supply, so filling it was mostly a problem of thirst.
Sikhs worship the pool itself as a god, so filling it was an attack on that god.
chat.meaning: Tradition says Guru Ram Das began the pool and Guru Arjan finished it and sang its praise. Sikhs answered its filling with a vow and kar seva.

notes: The index hook dates this to 1757; the script gives no year, per the claims rule. Abdali's commanders are not named (often Jahan Khan, with Timur Shah). Confirm.

Paraphrase of Ang 783 ('santa ke karaj aap khaloia...', 'dharat suhavi tal suhava vich amrit jal chhaia'): confirm the Ang and that the hymn is traditionally linked to the completion of the Amritsar sarovar.
'The city took its name from it: Amritsar, the pool of amrit' is the standard explanation of the name; confirm under the claims rule or cut.
Guru Ram Das beginning the pool and Guru Arjan completing it and building the Harmandir in its center: confirm.
Baba Deep Singh's vow is mentioned only briefly, since year one (day 290) told the last ride; the next index days do not retell it either. Confirm placement.
Later kar seva of the sarovar is described without dates; confirm.
